title: In the living room
subtitle: sofa, armchair, remote control
summary: Name the furniture and the other things in a living room, and say what people do there in the evening.

lesson.heading: Furniture in the living room
lesson.text: You sit on a **sofa** with other people, or in an **armchair** on your own. In front of the sofa there is often a **coffee table**, and your books are on a **bookshelf**. The plural of bookshelf is **bookshelves**.

examples.text: Come and sit on the **sofa** with me.
Dad always sits in the same **armchair**.
Put your cup on the **coffee table**.
We need some more **bookshelves** in this room.

lesson.heading: Other things in the room
rows: you close them over the window at night
you press it to turn the light on or off
you put the plug in it
a small light on a table or on the floor
you look at it on the wall
you change TV channels with it
you listen to music on it

lesson.heading: Useful verbs
lesson.text: In the evening people **watch** television, **listen to** the radio or **listen to** music, **read** a book, or just **relax**. To relax means to rest and do nothing.

examples.text: This evening let's just **relax** at home.

lesson.heading: Expressions
lesson.text: We **switch** or **turn** things **on** and **off**, and we **close** the curtains when it gets dark. Ask someone to **pass** you the remote control when you want to change channels.

examples.text: *A:* It's getting dark. Can you **close the curtains**, please?
*B:* OK. And I'll **switch the light on**.
*A:* Thanks. Now can you **turn the radio off**? And **pass me the remote control**.
I want to **turn on** the TV. There's a good programme on.

lesson.text: **Furniture** is uncountable: *The furniture in my room is white* - not ~~are white~~ and not ~~furnitures~~.
You **listen to** music or the radio, but you **watch** TV. There is no *to* and no *at* with watch.

exercises.prompt: Somewhere you can put books: a ___.
exercises.explanation: Books go on a bookshelf. Two or more are bookshelves.

exercises.prompt: Somewhere two or three people can sit: a ___.
exercises.explanation: A sofa is for two or three people; an armchair is for one.

exercises.prompt: Somewhere you can put down your cup: a ___.
exercises.explanation: The low table in front of the sofa is a coffee table.

exercises.prompt: Something for changing channels on the TV: a ___.
exercises.explanation: You change channels with the remote control.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings on the left with the right endings.
It's dark now. Please ___ the curtains.
exercises.explanation: We close the curtains and open the curtains.

exercises.prompt: Something you can look at on the wall is a ___.
Something under your feet is a ___.
exercises.explanation: A carpet covers the floor. A small carpet is a rug.

exercises.prompt: Put each thing in the right group.

exercises.statement: I don't often listen the radio in the evening.
exercises.explanation: I don't often listen to the radio in the evening. We always say listen to something.

exercises.statement: I watched television all evening yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Correct. We watch television - there is no at.

exercises.statement: Liam has some very nice furnitures in his house.
exercises.explanation: Liam has some very nice furniture in his house. Furniture has no plural.

exercises.statement: This evening let's just relax us at home.
exercises.explanation: This evening let's just relax at home. Relax does not take us or ourselves.

exercises.prompt: Ask someone to close the curtains.
exercises.answer: Can you close the curtains, please?
exercises.explanation: It's getting dark - so we close the curtains.

exercises.prompt: Say that you are going to put the light on.
exercises.explanation: You can say switch the light on or switch on the light.
